title: Corbino-Enhanced Supersonic Acoustic-Emission Threshold in a GaAs Two-Dimensional Electron System
authors: A. D. Levin, A. S. Jaroshevich, Z. D. Kvon, V. A. Chitta, M. S. Aksenov, D. V. Dmitriev, A. K. Bakarov, G. M. Gusev
abstract: We report nonlinear differential-resistance measurements in a high-mobility GaAs/AlGaAs two-dimensional electron system patterned in a Corbino geometry. At zero magnetic field, $R_{\mathrm{diff}}(I_{dc})$ exhibits a pronounced polarity-selective threshold peak on the negative-current branch, gradually suppressed by a perpendicular magnetic field. We interpret the Corbino anomaly as a local Cherenkov-like threshold for acoustic phonon emission, enabled by the radial current concentration $j_r(r)=I/(2πr)$, which drives the local electron velocity above the sound velocity in a region adjacent to the inner contact. The polarity selectivity is attributed to Peltier heating and cooling, which modify the local thermal and boundary conditions near the contact, rather than to the kinematic threshold itself. Our results identify the Corbino geometry as a sensitive platform for probing local nonequilibrium electron--phonon processes in a high-mobility electron system within an independently established hydrodynamic-crossover regime and suggest that the inner Corbino contact can act as a geometry-defined source for supersonic acoustic emission.
summary: This experimental work uses Corbino geometry devices to study nonlinear electron transport in a 2DES. Researchers report a sharp, polarity-dependent resistance threshold linked to the emission of acoustic phonons when local electron velocities exceed the sound speed. The findings establish the Corbino geometry as a sensitive platform for investigating local, non-equilibrium electron-phonon interactions.
main_problem: The study investigates nonlinear electron transport and local nonequilibrium electron-phonon processes in a two-dimensional electron system.
main_result: A pronounced, polarity-selective threshold peak in the differential resistance is observed in the Corbino geometry, interpreted as the onset of supersonic acoustic phonon emission near the inner contact.
method: Nonlinear differential-resistance measurements ($R_{diff} = dV/dI$) are performed on GaAs/AlGaAs Corbino devices under varying bias currents and perpendicular magnetic fields.
model_or_system: The physical system is a high-mobility GaAs/AlGaAs two-dimensional electron system patterned into a Corbino geometry. The transport is analyzed using a hydrodynamic description, focusing on the radial current density $j_r(r) = I/(2\pi r)$.
key_observables: Polarity-selective threshold peak in $R_{diff}(I_{dc})$, suppression of the peak by a perpendicular magnetic field, and the diodicity parameter $D$.
important_parameters: High-mobility 2DES, Corbino geometry, local electron velocity relative to sound velocity, perpendicular magnetic field $B$.
main_assumptions: The anomaly is localized near the inner contact, and the hydrodynamic framework provides a useful context, though the results are not strictly limited to it.
figures_summary: Figures show the schematic of the Corbino geometry and the calculated radial flow profile; subsequent figures illustrate the temperature and magnetic field dependence of the threshold peak on the negative-current branch, contrasting this with symmetric Hall-bar measurements.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical setup and measurements, presents the observation of the polarity-selective threshold peak in Corbino devices, interprets this peak as a Cherenkov-like acoustic emission process enhanced by the geometry, and confirms the robustness of this effect against field reversal and wiring changes.
why_interesting: The study probes non-equilibrium transport phenomena where energy dissipation (via phonons) becomes a critical, measurable parameter, which is relevant to understanding energy flow in quantum conductors.
